definitions.gloss: seal registration; registering a personal seal with the government
definitions.explanation: The process of officially registering a personal seal with the local municipal government. Once registered, the seal becomes a {実印|じついん} and can be used for important legal transactions.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}したら{印鑑登録|いんかんとうろく}をし{直|なお}す{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: You need to re-register your seal when you move.

examples.japanese: {印鑑登録|いんかんとうろく}は{市区町村|しくちょうそん}の{窓口|まどぐち}で{行|おこな}います。
examples.english: Seal registration is done at your local municipal office.

examples.japanese: {印鑑登録|いんかんとうろく}には{身分証明書|みぶんしょうめいしょ}が{必要|ひつよう}です。
examples.english: ID is required for seal registration.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{印鑑|いんかん} (seal) + {登録|とうろく} (registration)

REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS:
- {本人|ほんにん}{確認|かくにん}{書類|しょるい} - ID documents
- {登録|とうろく}する{印鑑|いんかん} - the seal to register
- {登録|とうろく}{手数料|てすうりょう} - registration fee (varies by municipality)

AFTER REGISTRATION:
You receive an {印鑑登録証|いんかんとうろくしょう} (registration card). This card is needed to obtain {印鑑証明書|いんかんしょうめいしょ} (seal certificate) when required for official transactions.

SEAL REQUIREMENTS:
{登録|とうろく}できる{印鑑|いんかん}:
- Size: usually 8mm-25mm
- Material: durable ({木|き}, {角|つの}, {象牙|ぞうげ}, チタン, etc.)
- Clear impression
- Shows registrant's name

{登録|とうろく}できない{印鑑|いんかん}:
- Mass-produced (100{円|えん}ショップ type)
- Rubber stamps
- Damaged or unclear impressions

IMPORTANT NOTES:
- One person can register only one seal
- Registration is tied to your {住民票|じゅうみんひょう} address
- Must re-register when moving to a new municipality
